definition: To become less intense or severe.
example: After Auntie exposed his secret Instagram poetry account at dinner, the humiliation refused to abate for three straight Eid gatherings.
mnemonic: Think: 'A bait.' Bro threw emotional bait into the family WhatsApp, expecting sympathy, but after 400 unread messages and one angry voice note from his mom, the drama finally started to abate like a dying boss battle.

definition: To secretly run away or disappear.
example: The waiter put the bill on the table, everyone looked down at their phones for two seconds, and Khalid had already absconded into the parking lot like he'd been training for this moment his whole life.
mnemonic: ABS-GONE. Imagine a ripped gym bro with glowing six-pack abs borrowing your power bank for 'just one minute' after Taraweeh. You blink once. He's gone. The power bank is gone. His Instagram is deleted. Witnesses say they saw him sprinting into the night like a Marvel post-credit scene.

definition: To deliberately avoid or refuse something.
example: He tried to abstain from online shopping during Ramadan, then bought a mechanical keyboard at 2:13 AM because it had 'thocky switches.'
mnemonic: Abstain sounds like 'apps stain.' Every time bro says he'll abstain from TikTok, another 6-hour screen-time stain appears on his soul.

definition: Existing as an idea rather than a concrete thing.
example: His explanation of why he ghosted her was so abstract that even the philosophy majors looked exhausted.
mnemonic: Abstract = 'ABSTRACT.' Imagine a shredded philosophy student flexing six-pack abs while explaining love using quantum mechanics and three Arabic quotes nobody asked for.

definition: Extremely bad or terrible.
example: His attempt at flirting was abysmal; he called her 'sis' halfway through the conversation and spiritually never recovered.
mnemonic: Abysmal sounds like 'abyss mall.' Imagine falling into a giant underground mall where every store sells failed exam papers, expired shawarma, and screenshots of your cringe texts.

definition: In a way that matches the situation.
example: Dad found the gaming PC receipt and adjusted his level of disappointment accordingly.
mnemonic: A CORDINGLY. Picture your strict dad holding the Wi-Fi cord. He checks your GPA: 3.9? He plugs in a new gaming PC. He checks your GPA: 1.9? He yanks the cord out of the wall. The cord acts ACCORDINGLY to the situation.

definition: Something gained or obtained.
example: His newest acquisition was a $300 chair that somehow made him feel like productivity itself would descend from the heavens.
mnemonic: Acquisition = 'a quiz I shun.' Bro avoids every quiz all semester but proudly acquires RGB lights like he's building NASA Mission Control.

definition: Sharp skill in making decisions or judgments.
example: The scammer texted, 'Congratulations! You won an iPhone.' Grandma almost clicked it, but Dad took one look and said, 'Brother, even the grammar is broke.' That level of acumen saved the whole family.
mnemonic: Acumen = 'IQ, man!' Picture your friend staring at a menu, instantly finding the cheapest item with the biggest portion, calculating tax, splitting the bill, catching the waiter adding an extra drink, and exposing the fake 70% discount. Everyone at the table just turns and goes, 'IQ, man... IQ.'

definition: To adjust to new conditions.
example: After moving into the dorm, he adapted quickly: noise-canceling headphones, instant noodles, and emotional numbness.
mnemonic: Adapt = 'a dad.' Desi dads adapt instantly. New country? Same slippers. Snowstorm? Same sandals. Economic collapse? Still turning off unnecessary lights.

definition: Very skilled or proficient.
example: She was so adept at spotting lies that he started sweating before even opening WhatsApp.
mnemonic: Adept sounds like 'a debt.' Your Gym Bro became adept at hiding Amazon packages because he was already $700 in keyboard debt.

definition: Good enough for a particular need.
example: Bro studied one night before the final, guessed half the MCQs, and somehow crawled out with exactly 50%. It wasn't impressive. It was merely adequate.
mnemonic: Adequate = 'ADD A QUOTE.' Your essay is complete garbage, so five minutes before the deadline you slap in a random Einstein quote, make the title bold, and submit. The professor sighs and gives you a C+. Not good. Just... adequate.

definition: To warn or scold firmly.
example: The imam gently admonished the brothers in the back who were ranking shawarma spots during the khutbah.
mnemonic: Admonish = 'a demon-ish.' Imagine your mother appearing silently behind you at 3 AM while you're gaming, delivering a demon-ish lecture about your destroyed sleep schedule.

definition: To make something impure by adding inferior material.
example: That suspicious cafeteria mango juice was so adulterated it tasted like sadness mixed with battery acid.
mnemonic: Adulterate = 'adult-irate.' Imagine angry adults secretly watering down biryani sauce at weddings to feed 900 extra guests.

definition: The arrival or beginning of something important.
example: The advent of AI note-taking apps turned every lazy student into a fake productivity guru overnight.
mnemonic: Advent = 'ad-venture.' Picture influencers celebrating the advent of Ramadan by posting cinematic coffee montages at suhoor like it's a Netflix trailer.

definition: Characterized by conflict or opposition.
example: The negotiation between him and his little sister over the Wi-Fi password became deeply adversarial by midnight.
mnemonic: Adversarial = 'ad versus Ariel.' Imagine two Disney princesses screaming legal threats at each other over group project credit.

definition: A person who supports something strongly; to support publicly.
example: He became a passionate advocate for naps after accidentally sleeping through an entire online lecture and feeling spiritually healed.
mnemonic: Advocate = 'ad-vote-cat.' Picture a political cat campaigning aggressively for longer Eid naps and mandatory shawarma breaks.

definition: Concerned with beauty or visual style.
example: His room looked aesthetic online, but outside the camera frame there were three plates, two dumbbells, and a collapsing mental state.
mnemonic: Aesthetic = 'A' is thick. Imazine a bold/thick letter 'A' that looks thick

definition: Fake or exaggerated behavior meant to impress others.
example: His British accent during presentations was such an affectation that even the professor looked personally offended.
mnemonic: Affectation = 'acting for attention.' Imagine a guy watching one season of Peaky Blinders, then showing up to class with a fake British accent, fake cigar, and calling the professor 'mate.'

definition: To have enough money or ability for something.
example: He could not afford both textbooks and emotional stability, so he chose coffee and chaos instead.
mnemonic: Afford = 'a Ford.' Imagine a university student buying a giant Ford truck while surviving on instant noodles and mom's dua.

definition: To make something appear greater or more important.
example: Bro aggrandized his one-week gym streak like he had conquered ancient civilizations.
mnemonic: Aggrandize = 'a grand eyes.' Picture a guy widening his eyes dramatically while describing how he 'basically built the entire app' after fixing one typo.

definition: To disturb, upset, or stir up.
example: Remember how Sheikh Hasina agitated the whole gen z calling them Rajakarer Bacca?
mnemonic: Agitate = agy-tate. Imagine agy/old Andrew Tate ranting in online with his rage bate.

definition: Cheerful willingness and quickness.
example: The class showed absolutely no enthusiasm for the lecture, but the second the professor announced, 'Attendance is already marked,' everyone left with unbelievable alacrity.
mnemonic: Think: 'ALL, ACT READY!' Someone yells, 'Free pizza in the common room!' Suddenly twenty broke college students teleport out of nowhere carrying paper plates. Nobody asks questions. They move with pure alacrity.

definition: To reduce pain or difficulty.
example: One perfectly timed meme in the group chat somehow alleviated the collective despair before finals.
mnemonic: Alleviate = 'Ali-leviate.' Imagine your friend Ali arriving with iced coffee and biryani exactly when your code crashes for the seventh time.

definition: To hint at something indirectly.
example: She kept alluding to 'someone immature' while staring directly at him across the study table.
mnemonic: Allude = 'a loot.' Imagine your friend casually alluding to the fact you still owe him money by loudly discussing bankruptcy near your parents.

definition: A noisy argument or fight.
example: One guy microwaved fish at 2 A.M. in the hostel kitchen, and within thirty seconds the whole floor was involved in an altercation.
mnemonic: Think: ALTER + CATION. Somebody ALTERED the biryani order from 'extra chicken' to 'extra salad.' Suddenly two uncles are pointing fingers, one aunt is crying, three cousins are recording for Instagram, and grandma is yelling, 'I knew this family would split over food!' That's an altercation.

definition: Open to more than one interpretation.
example: Her text saying, 'Do whatever you want,' was so ambiguous that bro spent three business days consulting three friends and still got it wrong.
mnemonic: 'Am-big-you-us.' You, her, him, and two backup options are all confused about the relationship situation like it's a badly written Netflix plot.

definition: Having strong desire for success or achievement.
example: His ambitious Ramadan schedule included tahajjud, gym, coding, meal prep, journaling, and somehow only collapsed by Day 2.
mnemonic: Ambitious = 'ham-bee-shus.' Imagine a hyperactive bee in a suit juggling five startups, memorizing Qur'an, and trading crypto before sunrise.
